gaps.what: Neutral monster art was never reviewed. Nine monster GLBs (glasshorn, gloamoth, gloamoth_little, resinback, stilltusk, stilltusk_young, stray_numeral, stray_tick, sunsplinter) are unchanged since 2026-10-14 (git 9c5b7e5a / 6adfa7a2). No closing lens, fighter review or wave scored how finished they are. Sunsplinter, an epic objective, renders as a cluster of grey boxes. Glasshorn and Stray Numeral render as near-untextured off-white solids.
gaps.why: Gauge: in LoL every jungle camp and epic monster is finished art at champion level. The owner's bar is League-level graphics. E1 made the FRAY props from the same Oct 14 vintage a major, but the monsters fell between lenses: env checked only their fog multiplier (0.34-0.39), audio only their cues, and originality only Longshade's plate. Their in-game finish is unknown, and so is their sensitivity read: Stray Numeral has two dark dot holes on its head. Evidence: art/renders/units/{sunsplinter,glasshorn,stray_numeral,gloamoth,stilltusk,resinback}.png (Oct 14, same timestamp as the GLBs); crops _harness/_shots/closing_critic_monsters_oct14_renders.png and _sheet.png.
gaps.howToMeasure: Give the 10 monsters (with Longshade) a per-unit review using the fighter-review method: a three_snapshot sheet; shot_map at each camp and pit at a t when they are up, at 28.5 m; face high-pass against an Art 2.0 structure (env E1 method: Needle hp 19.8, flagstone 2.93); L*/chroma separation from the camp floor; silhouette IoU between camps; a horror/face read on each. Score a 'neutral units' row in the scorecard.

gaps.what: The camera was not measured. The owner lists camera, but the closing scorecard has no camera row. The only camera evidence is m4 (0 shake layers, camJitter 0). r12's 'Camera: Matches' verdict is carried forward from r12 itself. src/render/camera.ts:18 still has pitch 52, vertical fov 26, distance 28.5 m and zoom 24.5-33 m. Nobody re-measured fighter on-screen height for all 16, edge-pan speed, the lock, semi-lock and free modes, re-centre, the scout key, follow smoothing, or the camera on death and respawn.
gaps.why: r12 calls the camera a fairness system, and it is one of the owner's named pillars. Fighter scales and bar clearance changed in Art 2.0. For example, Kemdo's crown is 2.121 m, 114 px at 1080p (closing/fighters/kemdo.json). So the 105-130 px gauge (r12 §2) needs a fresh check on the final roster.
gaps.howToMeasure: Per-fighter screen height at 28.5 m and 1080p, from value_probe fighter masks or shot_fighter, for all 16 base models plus skins; gate 105-130 px. Run `node _harness/probe_camera_edge.ts --out _harness/_reports/closing_camera_edge.json`. A scripted real-client pan test should time edge-pan px/s, the re-centre key, the lock toggle and the respawn re-centre, and compare against the r04 §6 behaviours.

gaps.what: Input-to-action feel was never measured: click to move marker to first motion, attack-move, the wind-up cancel window, turn rate, foot sliding and locomotion blending. These are r12 §6's own open items ('foot planting, turn speed and locomotion blending'), and no closing JSON measures them (0 hits for latency, turn rate or foot sliding).
gaps.why: 'Attacks feel League-level' depends on how fast an order takes effect and how cleanly units move, not only on VFX. Combat measured wind-up length (0.21-0.26 s), never responsiveness. Gauge: LoL acknowledges an order on the next frame and starts motion within a server tick (about 33 ms at 30 Hz).
gaps.howToMeasure: Real-client harness that sends 50 CDP mouse orders (move, attack, attack-move, and a move during a wind-up) and logs, by rAF timestamp, the frame the marker draws and the frame the fighter's position or animation changes. Report p50/p95 in ms. From the GLB and sim speed, report foot-slip per fighter run cycle (planted-foot world speed) and turn rate in deg/s.

gaps.what: The combat live captures cover only 8 of 16 fighters. closing_combat_kits.json covers marund, ilsheta, sukri, nurrow and dunsom; closing_combat_c_kits.json covers hesmi, tunlan and burdam: 32 of 64 casts. Ardit, Ervet, Kemdo, Lisvel, Odrum, Rishal, Ulkro and Vashil have no live evidence for f0 telegraphs, anticipation pixels, victim flash, ult envelope or distortion. gaps.why: M1, M3, M13 and m5 are marked Closed or Partly for all 16 fighters. For the 8 uncaptured fighters those statuses rest on a content walk alone. The owner's 'special moves at League level' is unproven for half the roster. Only Hesmi and Kemdo got the ult-core (x2.3) check.

gaps.what: Audio runtime claims were not re-verified, and the r12 §6 'audio sync' gap was closed on the wrong measure. The audio verifier states 'Not re-run: a real Chrome capture of my own'. So the -19 LUFS master, the ambience at -28.1 LUFS, the M2 CC-sound path and the M6 procs all rest on the reviewer's capture and probes. The review itself says pw.mjs audio probes meter silence on this Mac (CW2 done-when), so in-browser metered gates can pass vacuously here. 'r12-§6 audio sync: closed' cites file onset only: cues reach -20 dB within 10.6 ms of the file start (closing_audio_verify_onset.txt). That says nothing about the in-engine latency from the impact frame to sound out.
gaps.why: Sound is an owner pillar, and audio is the weakest dimension (6.5). A/V offset is what a player feels as 'hits land'. Industry detectability (ITU-R BT.1359) is about 45 ms audio-early or 125 ms audio-late. Closing a sync gap on the file's own onset is a stale proxy.
gaps.howToMeasure: A real-Chrome capture on the fake output device (the closing_audio_tool_open.mjs method). Inject 50 timed hits and record the rAF timestamp of each impact frame next to the captured audio stream. Cross-correlate and report the p50/p95 offset, including AudioContext.outputLatency. Have the verifier re-run the RIFT loudness capture once.

gaps.what: The HUD ON PAR verdict (exactly 8.0) rests partly on unmeasured states that are marked Closed. M4 is Closed, but 'Not enough {resource}' was never seen live: both runs drew Tally fighters, and the reviewer's crop closing_hud_A05_refused_resource.png shows no caption in frame. m1 is Closed with the 250 ms ready wash and the active border untimed. m2 is Closed, but only the ace banners were timed: multikill, shutdown and streak banners were not. r12's 'Accessibility: Exceeds' (colourblind alternates) was carried forward with no check. BRIDGE and FRAY minimaps were not viewed.
gaps.why: The score sits on the par line, with 10 confirmed minors already. The measured core reproduces (see spotChecks), but every unmeasured state is a HUD surface a League player sees in a normal match.
gaps.howToMeasure: A live capture with a mana fighter (res to 0, press Q) for the refusal caption. A frame-timed ready wash (expect 250 ms) and active border. Injected multikill, shutdown and streak events, checking banner order and latency (hud-c1 FIFO). Deutan, protan and tritan HUD and minimap shots with ΔE between relationship colours. BRIDGE and FRAY minimap shots.

gaps.what: The sensitivity sweep is incomplete, and its geometry is inconsistent. (a) The Wick check used close-up renders of shieldwick, glimwick and brightwick only (closing_originality_verify_wick_closeups.png). The Greatwick eye-pair surfaced only by chance in the HUD verifier's live lane frame. No live sweep covers all 4 Wick kinds × 2 teams (plus base greatwick.glb) at 28.5 m on both lane headings. (b) The Hooded Lamp ward (ruling-5 finial fix, hooded_lamp.glb 1667afb3, Oct 28) and the 10 monsters got no closing sensitivity look. (c) There is no numeric crown gate. vashil.json says the other hooded heads are '3 to 9 times blunter', but my sweep of all 48 fighter GLBs with the verifier's own tool gives a different picture. Lisvel is 10.7 cm at 5 cm, only 1.6x Vashil's 6.7 cm. Kemdo's crown is sharper than Vashil's at 1 cm (6.6 vs 7.3 cm), with 8.1 cm at 3 cm. Ulkro is 5.5 cm at 1 cm and 7.0 cm at 3 cm, the same as Vashil. All skins share their base head (_harness/_reports/closing_critic_crown_radius.txt). From behind at eye level, Kemdo's brown hood shows a soft peak much like Vashil's (_harness/_shots/closing_critic_hood_backviews_vashil_ulkro_kemdo.png).
gaps.why: Pointed hoods are blocker class anywhere in the game. The Vashil blocker leans on a geometric uniqueness that the numbers do not support. Either the rule is really about Vashil's pale colour plus the pointed-arch front rim, and should be written that way, or Kemdo and Ulkro need the same gameplay-camera rear check. The 15-of-16-clean claim is therefore unverified.
gaps.howToMeasure: One crown metric run over every fighter, skin, Wick, ward and monster GLB: geo2.mjs fit radius at 1, 3 and 5 cm, plus the dome-width ratio. Set one threshold in owner_rulings.md. Take gameplay-camera rear and three-quarter-rear captures at 28.5 m for Kemdo, Ulkro, Vashil and Lisvel on all skins. Do a live 8-heading Wick sweep that includes the Greatwick on both teams.

gaps.what: The originality audit never covered UI layout or sound design. Closing and final originality.json have 0 mentions of layout, HUD, minimap, scoreboard, audio, sound or music. The owner's rule bans copying any 'UI layout detail'. The in-match bar was never classified as genre convention or one-to-one mapping. It has a portrait with level at the left, Q W E R plus D and F, a 2×3 item grid numbered 1-6 and currency under the items (_harness/_shots/closing_hud_A05_refused_resource.png). Signature UI sounds (queue pop, level-up, recall, ready check) were never compared either.
gaps.why: Originality is scored 7.8 on names, numbers, rules and character visuals only. Layout and sound are where a League player most readily spots borrowing, and owner ruling 4's 'no rule may map one to one' should apply to presentation too.
gaps.howToMeasure: A layout audit against r04 §2's LoL layout notes: slot order, relative positions and grid shape of the Dial Bar, minimap corner, scoreboard columns and shop tree. Classify each as shared genre convention (shared with Dota 2, SMITE, HotS) or one-to-one. Describe the signature UI cues (pitch contour and envelope) against r07's descriptions of LoL's cues. Capture no LoL audio.

gaps.what: Bot micro-quality was never measured. Gameplay measured only macro numbers: takedowns, last-hit share, lane presence, pacing. Nothing covers r09 §3.5-3.9: kiting, retreat thresholds, focus fire, skillshot lead and dodge, recall timing. Bots were never measured against a human seat. BRIDGE, FRAY, practice and G5-G8 were accepted from the reviewer without a re-run (gameplay.json gapStatus G5-G8, g3).
gaps.why: The owner wants League-level bots. A bot that farms at 52-56 % but never dodges a telegraph or punishes a human reads as tier-below, even if CL-1 is fixed.
gaps.howToMeasure: Instrument the sim soak per tier: skillshot hit rate, dodge rate against telegraphed areas, share of deaths taken below the retreat threshold, focus share on the lowest-EHP target, and HP at recall. Add a scripted passive human seat to measure bot aggression toward the player at 3-8 min. Re-run pacing and soak once on BRIDGE and FRAY.

gaps.what: The LoL gauge behind the only Gameplay major (CL-1) comes from memory. 'About 6 kills per team by 10:00' and 'almost always a first blood before 10:00' are unsourced (closing_parity_review.md §e). VALE's first-blood median of 4.3-4.5 min may already sit in LoL's range. The major then rests on kill volume (1.75-1.90 takedowns by 10:00) and on 2-5 of 20 games with none.
gaps.why: The CL-1 severity and the Gameplay 6.0 score depend on that number, and the review's own evidence rule asks for a cited gauge.
gaps.howToMeasure: Source kills at 10:00 and first-blood time from a public solo-queue dataset. One example is Kaggle's 'League of Legends Diamond Ranked Games (10 min)', about 10k Diamond-Master games with per-team kills at 10:00. Then re-grade CL-1 against the measured mean and spread.

gaps.what: The B4 gate measures one fixed 10 s view. Match-density frame pacing has no real-time gate and no idle-machine number.
gaps.why: The closing gate's fixed view is about 226-257k triangles and 167-174 draws. The match-peak step reaches 461-484k triangles and 265-273 draws, but runs the sim at 4x and only checks counts. My real-time run (spotChecks, B4) shows 60 fps holds at the 461k peak, but 4.7 % of wall-seconds fall under 58 frames, worst second 23, and that run is confounded by a machine load that rose to about 7.7. LoL gauge: 1080p60 is the floor.
gaps.howToMeasure: Add the real-time step to the gate: `node _harness/perf_1080.mjs --prod --no-build --match-only --match-scale 1 --match-min 19`, run at load < 3 with no other heavy slot held. Gate at 99 % or more of wall-seconds at 58+ frames and no second under 45, and record the worst seconds (748, 871, 1089 s in seed 7) with Renderer.profile to separate hitches from load.

spotChecks.claim: B4 is closed: perf_1080 --prod GATE PASS, High 60.1 fps, 0 of 601 frames dropped, p95 16.7 ms ('frame pacing at League tier').
spotChecks.result: REPRODUCED at the fixed view, and holds at teamfight density in real time, with caveats. (1) Fixed view at another moment: perf_1080 --prod --q high --t 1080 gave GATE PASS: 60.1 fps, 0 of 601 frames dropped, p95 16.8 ms, p99 16.8 ms, 226k triangles, 167 draws, idle window (load 2.86 to 2.65). (2) New: a whole RIFT match in real time (match step at sim scale 1, 0:00-19:00, High 1080p, camera on the autopilot fighter). Median 61 frames per wall-second, mean 60.1. The 461k-triangle teamfight peak at 18:00.6 held 61 frames. 4.7 % of 1,126 seconds fell under 58 frames, 1.2 % under 50 and 0.7 % under 40; the worst second was 23 frames (12:28, 271k triangles, 73 VFX), plus 38-39 frames at 18:09-18:10 (260 draws). The machine load rose from about 2.7 to 7.7 during the run (other agents), so these dips are not proof of a build defect. B4 'Closed' stands. 'Frame pacing at League tier' is supported at the default preset, but not yet proven under real match density on an idle machine.

spotChecks.claim: Sensitivity is clean on 15 of 16 fighters, and Vashil's crown is uniquely sharp ('the roster's other hooded or wrapped heads are 3 to 9 times blunter', closing/fighters/vashil.json).
spotChecks.result: NOT SUPPORTED by the verifier's own metric. I ran the head-weighted crown fit radius on all 48 fighter GLBs (skins share their base head). Vashil: 7.3 / 7.0 / 6.7 cm at 1 / 3 / 5 cm. Kemdo (hood): 6.6 / 8.1 / 10.0, sharper than Vashil at 1 cm. Ulkro (hood): 5.5 / 7.0 / 9.4, the same as Vashil at 3 cm. Lisvel: 14.5 / 11.9 / 10.7, which is 1.6x, not 3x. Odrum's cap knob (2.1 cm at 1 cm), Rishal's ridge blade (1.9-2.8 cm, owner ruling 3) and Marund Long Evening (3.0-4.1 cm) are sharper still, but they are not hoods. From behind at eye level, Kemdo's hood shows a soft peak comparable to Vashil's. The difference is colour (brown, not pale) and Vashil's pointed-arch front rim. This does not make Kemdo or Ulkro blockers, because the gameplay-camera rear read is unmeasured. It does mean the 15-of-16 claim and the Vashil-only blocker rest on a rule with no stated threshold.
spotChecks.evidence: _harness/_reports/closing_critic_crown_radius.txt (tool _harness/_reports/closing_vashil_tools/geo2.mjs, R=((min(w,d)/2)^2+d^2)/(2d)); compare _harness/_reports/closing_vashil_verify_crown.txt; _harness/_shots/closing_critic_hood_backviews_vashil_ulkro_kemdo.png (from art/renders/fighters/<id>/turntable.png).
